original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

Use the signed invoice preflight where its boundary contract agrees; an inconclusive concave comparison is not a power crossing. Stop if an optimistic complete budget fails at the chosen target or native delivery remains unspecified.

actual_scope: Determine the maximum deletion threshold for the global quadratic-extension property on P112 (open next question of PR5697): the largest k such that, for every X in P112 with |X|<=k, the kernel of the all-live-frame incidence on P112 minus X equals the 35-dimensional space of trace-zero quadratic restrictions.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a priced decoder change. This package answers the explicitly open threshold question left by PR5697, a structural input to the P112 rigidity and decoder line; it is a side result with no supplier, invoice or kappa.
bottleneck_link: Side result. It fixes the exact deletion range in which the uniform quadratic-extension argument of PR5697 can be reused for P112 incidence and decoder rigidity work. It prices nothing.
stop_rule: Stop at the first exactly certified eight-deletion failure; with PR5697 this settles the threshold. Do not extend to a full classification of eight-deletion failures.
evidence: Finite exact certificate: for each of 14 explicit eight-line deletion sets the live-frame incidence has rational rank 62 on 104 lines, kernel dimension 42 > 35, so global quadratic extension fails at eight deletions. With PR5697 (extension for every |X|<=7, cited, not rechecked here) the maximum threshold is exactly 7. verify.py: exact Fraction elimination for all 14 octets, quadratic restriction dimension 35 on each live set, isolated-line structure, seven-subset rank controls and a damaged-octet control.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Classify all eight-deletion sets X in P112 for which global quadratic extension fails, up to the FRAME0 stabilizer of order 172032.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would show whether line isolation by a heavy-partner octet is the only failure mechanism at eight deletions, or whether rank loss without isolation also occurs.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the retained PR1650 orbit cover from seven to eight deletions and run the exact global rank test on each representative. A greedy eight-set found during this work has kernel 37 and is not one of the 14 octets.
open_questions.blocked_by: The eight-deletion orbit cover is not yet materialized; seven deletions already have 242802 representatives.

open_questions.question: Does the 7-dimensional excess persist as the maximum kernel excess over all eight-deletion sets, and what is the maximum excess as a function of |X| up to the injectivity limit |X|<=9?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A sharp excess profile bounds how many extra non-quadratic kernel directions a decoder or rigidity argument must handle after deletions.
open_questions.first_step: Search eight- and nine-deletion sets for kernel dimension above 42 with an exact rank test.
open_questions.blocked_by: No complete search is supplied here; any search result would be a search failure unless exhaustive.
